newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi court does not rule on tobacco suit.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi court does not rule on tobacco suit.

text.p: The Mississippi Supreme Court did not rule on Thursday on Gov. Kirk Fordice's challenge to a $940 million landmark tobacco lawsuit, despite speculation among investors on Wall Street.
Analysts said tobacco stocks were higher on expectations that a ruling favorable to the industry would be issued at 1330 CST/1930 GMT when the court customarily makes its decisions public.
"It did not come down," a spokeswoman for the clerk of court's office said after the day's rulings had been published.
Shares in Philip Morris Cos Inc, up 2-1/4 as the deadline approached, retreated from their peak after the news to trade 1-3/8 higher at 106-5/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.

Fordice, a Republican, has challenged the lawsuit brought by Democrat state Attorney General Mike Moore because it seeks compensation for state Medicaid funds spent treating poor people for smoking-related illnesses.
The governor claims that only he has the authority to bring lawsuits to recover Medicaid money since the state's division of Medicaid is under the control of his office.
Had the court ruled in Fordice's favor, Moore's lawsuit would have been limited to claims on behalf of charity hospital spending and the prohibition of cigarette advertising aimed at children.
